newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England raises official rates to 7.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England raises official rates to 7.0 percent.

text.p: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee raised official interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent on Thursday, the fourth increase in as many months.

"In the light of the prospect for domestic demand and on the basis of all the evidence currently available, the committee judges that today's rise is necessary to put the economy on track for achieving the inflation target of 2.5 percent looking two years ahead," the committee said in a statement.

It said it recognised that the strong pound was putting severe pressure on businesses exposed to international competition, but said the pound's strength was largely due to factors outside the influence of British policy-makers.
In an apparent hint to financial markets that it had no immediate plans for further rate rises, the committee said:
"Upward pressures on the exchange rate should be reduced by the perception that interest rates have reached a level consistent with the inflation target."

The pound, which has surged around 25 percent against major currencies in the past year, slipped nearly two pfennigs against the deutschemark after the rate move. It was quoted at 2.9948/58 marks compared with 3.0130/40 just beforehand.
London share prices advanced on the Monetary Policy Committee's statement, which was taken as a clear hint that monetary policy was not likely to be tightened again soon.
